summary: Sieve-based primality and divisor problems. The Sieve of Eratosthenes precomputes all primes up to N in O(N log log N); divisor counts come from trial division up to sqrt(n). Watch the classic sieve bugs: start crossing at i*i, cast i*i to long, and remember 0 and 1 are not prime.

thoughtProcess.title: Need primality for many numbers up to N? Sieve once, then O(1) lookups.
thoughtProcess.body: One boolean[] sieve of size N+1 answers every 'is x prime' in O(1). Per-number trial division (O(sqrt x) each) only wins for a few queries or very large single values.

thoughtProcess.title: Counting divisors? Loop to sqrt(n) and add divisors in pairs.
thoughtProcess.body: For each i with i*i <= n and n%i==0, i and n/i are both divisors (count 2, or 1 when i == n/i for a perfect square).

thoughtProcess.title: 'Sum of two primes' / Goldbach-style: sieve, then scan p and check N-p.
thoughtProcess.body: For each prime p <= N/2, if (N-p) is also prime you have a pair; sieve makes both checks O(1).

keyPatterns.name: Sieve of Eratosthenes
keyPatterns.when: All primes / prime flags up to N (N <= ~1e7)

keyPatterns.name: Divisor count in O(sqrt n)
keyPatterns.when: Count/lists divisors of a single number
keyPatterns.template: int c=0; for(int i=1;(long)i*i<=n;i++) if(n%i==0) c += (i==n/i)?1:2;

commonMistakes.title: Sieve inner loop starts at 2*i, or i*i in int
commonMistakes.why: Multiples below i*i are already crossed by smaller primes; and i*i overflows int near N=1e9, wrapping negative.

commonMistakes.title: Treating 0 or 1 as prime
commonMistakes.right: start the prime scan at i=2; comp[0]=comp[1]=true conceptually
commonMistakes.why: 0 and 1 are not prime; including them corrupts prime lists and Goldbach checks.

edgeCases: Sieve array must be size N+1 so index N is valid; the outer loop only needs i*i <= N.
n < 2 has no primes and 0 divisors-of-interest — guard tiny inputs.
Perfect squares: count the sqrt divisor once, not twice.
Very large single n with no upper bound: use O(sqrt n) trial division, not a sieve (memory).
